slot.brief: Rank C–O bond lengths / bond orders in species like CO, CO2, CO3^2−, HCOOH using resonance structures and formal bond order counting.

stem: Arrange the indicated C–O bonds in increasing order of bond length: in $\text{CO}$, $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{HCOO}^-$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$.

verdicts.working: Bond orders decrease in the sequence CO (3), CO₂ (2), HCOO⁻ (1.5 average), CO₃²⁻ (4/3 average); lower bond order corresponds to greater bond length.

working:
Average C–O bond orders: $\text{CO}=3$, $\text{CO}_2=2$, $\text{HCOO}^-=1.5$, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}=4/3$.\nBond length increases as bond order decreases.\nThus: $\text{CO} < \text{CO}_2 < \text{HCOO}^- < \text{CO}_3^{2-}$.

Independent check: Bond orders decrease in the sequence CO (3), CO₂ (2), HCOO⁻ (1.5 average), CO₃²⁻ (4/3 average); lower bond order corresponds to greater bond length.
solution:
Bond length decreases as bond order increases. The average C–O bond orders are $3$ in CO, $2$ in CO₂, $1.5$ in HCOO⁻ and $4/3$ in CO₃²⁻.
Hence, in increasing order of bond length: $\text{CO} < \text{CO}_2 < \text{HCOO}^- < \text{CO}_3^{2-}$.
